events.label: Holmes presents documents and a message to Watson at a winter night by the fire

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I have some papers here, which I really think, Watson, that it would be worth your while to glance over.

events.label: Holmes produces a tarnished cylinder from a drawer and undoes tape
Holmes hands Watson a short note scrawled on a half-sheet of slate-grey paper
The message is read by Justice of the Peace Trevor
Justice of the Peace Trevor is knocked down after reading the message
Watson reads the enigmatical message and Holmes chuckles
Holmes tells Watson he looks bewildered

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You look a little bewildered

events.label: Watson asks Holmes why he said there were particular reasons to study the case

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: But why did you say just now that there were very particular reasons why I should study this case?

events.label: Holmes replies that it was the first case he was engaged in

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Because it was the first in which I was ever engaged.

events.label: Holmes asks Watson whether he has heard of Victor Trevor

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You never heard me talk of Victor Trevor?

events.label: Watson is described as being a guest of Victor Trevor for a month during the long vacation
Holmes describes that Trevor senior receives port and young Trevor begins discussing habits of observation and inference
Trevor senior tells Holmes that he can deduce something from him

communicates.speaker: trevor_senior
communicates.content: I'm an excellent subject, if you can deduce anything from me.

events.label: Trevor senior says that after breaking up a poaching gang, they swore to knife them and Sir Edward Holly was attacked

communicates.speaker: trevor_senior
communicates.content: when we broke up that poaching gang, they swore to knife us, and Sir Edward Holly has actually been attacked. I've always been on my guard since then, though I have no idea how you know it.

events.label: Sailor Hudson is introduced to Mr. Trevor at the door after a maid announces a visitor
Victor Trevor runs into the house after seeing the sailor Hudson on the lawn
Victor Trevor orders Hudson to go to the kitchen for food and drink and says he will find him a situation

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: Go into the kitchen, and you will get food and drink. I have no doubt that I shall find you a situation.

events.label: Hudson tells Trevor he wants a rest and mentions being off a two-yearer in an eight-knot tramp, short-handed

communicates.speaker: hudson_seaman
communicates.content: I'm just off a two-yearer in an eight-knot tramp, short-handed at that, and I wants a rest. I thought I'd get it either with Mr. Beddoes or with you.

events.label: Hudson slouches off after being told to go for friends
Trevor is found dead drunk on the dining-room sofa an hour later
Watson receives a telegram urging him to return to Donnithorpe
Watson returns to Donnithorpe once more after the telegram
Victor Trevor meets Watson at the station by dog-cart
Victor Trevor tells Watson that the governor is dying of apoplexy and nervous shock

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: The governor is dying. Apoplexy. Nervous shock, He's been on the verge all day. I doubt if we shall find him alive.

events.label: Victor Trevor says the devil himself is responsible and blames accursed Hudson for all trouble

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: It was the devil, Holmes. Yes, it was the devil himself. We have not had a peaceful hour since—not one. The governor has never held up his head from that evening, and now the life has been crushed out of him and his heart broken, all through this accursed Hudson.

events.label: Victor Trevor describes Hudson's role in his house, including being intrustive, receiving complaints, and taking the boat and best gun
Victor Trevor turns Hudson out of the room by the shoulders after an insolent reply
Trevor senior asks Victor Trevor to apologize to Hudson

communicates.speaker: trevor_senior
communicates.content: asked me whether I would mind apologising to Hudson.

events.label: Victor Trevor refuses to apologize to Hudson and asks his father how Hudson is allowed such liberties

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: I refused, as you can imagine, and asked my father how he could allow such a wretch to take such liberties with himself and his household.

events.label: Trevor senior tells Victor he will let him know harm that may come to his father and promises to see he knows

communicates.speaker: trevor_senior
communicates.content: it is all very well to talk, but you don't know how I am placed. But you shall know, Victor. I'll see that you shall know, come what may.

events.label: Hudson announces his intention to leave and run down to Mr. Beddoes

communicates.speaker: hudson_seaman
communicates.content: I've had enough of Norfolk. I'll run down to Mr. Beddoes in Hampshire. He'll be as glad to see me as you were, I daresay.

events.label: Trevor senior urges Hudson to not go away with an unkind spirit

communicates.speaker: trevor_senior
communicates.content: You're not going away in an unkind spirit, Hudson, I hope

events.label: Trevor senior claims he has not had his 'pology from Hudson

communicates.speaker: trevor_senior
communicates.content: I've not had my 'pology

events.label: Trevor senior tells Victor Trevor to acknowledge using Hudson roughly

communicates.speaker: trevor_senior
communicates.content: Victor, you will acknowledge that you have used this worthy fellow rather roughly

events.label: Victor Trevor replies that they have shown extraordinary patience

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: On the contrary, I think that we have both shown extraordinary patience towards him

events.label: Hudson seaman snarls
Hudson seaman slouches out of the room and leaves the house
Trevor senior paces his room at night
A letter arrives for Trevor senior
Trevor senior reads the letter, claps hands to head, and runs in circles
Victor Trevor observes Trevor senior has a stroke
Dr. Fordham comes over
Victor Trevor says Trevor senior is put to bed with paralysis spreading and no return of consciousness

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: We put him to bed; but the paralysis has spread, he has shown no sign of returning consciousness, and I think that we shall hardly find him alive

events.label: Watson cries out asking what was in the letter

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: What then could have been in this letter to cause so dreadful a result?

events.label: Victor Trevor states there is nothing but the inexplicable part of the letter

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: Nothing. There lies the inexplicable part of it. The message was absurd and trivial.

events.label: Trevor senior's household blinds are drawn down as Victor Trevor and Watson come around the avenue
A gentleman in black emerges as Trevor senior's friend’s face convulses with grief
Victor Trevor asks when it happened

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: Almost immediately after you left.

events.label: Victor Trevor asks whether Trevor senior recovered consciousness

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: Did he recover consciousness?

events.label: Watson replies that consciousness returned for an instant before the end

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: For an instant before the end.

events.label: Victor Trevor asks if there was any message for him

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: Any message for me?

events.label: Watson reports the only message: papers in the back drawer of the Japanese cabinet

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: Only that the papers were in the back drawer of the Japanese cabinet.

events.label: Victor Trevor and the doctor go upstairs to the chamber of death while Watson stays in the study
Watson decides to see the letter
A weeping maid brings a lamp and Trevor brings papers to Watson in the room
Trevor sits opposite Watson, draws the lamp, and hands over a short note on a grey sheet
Trevor reads a note stating supply of game for London is going steadily up

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: The supply of game for London is going steadily up,

events.label: Trevor reads a note stating Head-keeper Hudson has been told to receive orders for fly paper and preservation of a hen pheasant's life

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: Head-keeper Hudson, we believe, has been now told to receive all orders for fly paper and for preservation of your hen pheasant's life.

events.label: Watson reads the warning that the game is up, Hudson has told all, and Fly for your life

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: The game is up. Hudson has told all. Fly for your life.

events.label: Victor Trevor sinks his face into his shaking hands
Watson obtains papers drawn up by Trevor senior and prepared to be read
Victor Trevor instructs Watson to take the papers and read them to him

communicates.speaker: victor_trevor
communicates.content: Here is the statement... I found it in the Japanese cabinet, as he told the doctor. Take it and read it to me, for I have neither the strength nor the courage to do it myself.

events.label: The endorsed papers are described as a letter about the bark Gloria Scott voyage and destruction
Endorsed letter begins addressing the son about approaching disgrace and urges honesty

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: My dear, dear son,—Now that approaching disgrace begins to darken the closing years of my life, I can write with all truth and honesty...

events.label: Endorsed letter states the author's name is James Armitage

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: My name, dear lad, is not Trevor.

events.label: Endorsed letter states James Armitage entered a London banking house, was convicted, and sentenced to transportation

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: As Armitage I was convicted of breaking my country's laws, and was sentenced to transportation.

events.label: Endorsed letter states the author was chained as a felon on the barque Gloria Scott bound for Australia

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: On my twenty-third birthday I found myself chained as a felon with thirty-seven other convicts in 'tween-decks of the barque Gloria Scott, bound for Australia.

events.label: Endorsed letter states the ship set sail from Falmouth with nearly a hundred souls

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: Nearly a hundred souls were in her, all told, when we set sail from Falmouth.

events.label: Endorsed letter states the author finds a neighbor cut an opening in the board

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: found that he had managed to cut an opening in the board which separated us.

events.label: Endorsed letter has the neighbor introduce himself as Jack Prendergast and threaten future blessing

communicates.speaker: jack_prendergast
communicates.content: I'm Jack Prendergast... You'll learn to bless my name before you've done with me.

events.label: Endorsed letter states an explosion occurs in the captain's cabin and the chaplain stands with a smoking pistol while the crew seize mates
Wilson knocks a locker and pulls out brown sherry
Brown sherry is poured into tumblers
Muskets fire and smoke fills the saloon
The saloon is left as a shambles after the smoke clears
Wilson and eight others are wriggling on the floor, with blood and brown sherry on the table
Prendergast bellows and rushes for the door with those left alive
The fleeing group runs out onto the poop where the lieutenant and ten of his men are found
Swing skylights above the saloon table are open and fire through the slit
The group gets on the attackers before they load, and the fight ends in five minutes
Prendergast picks up soldiers and throws them overboard alive or dead
A horribly wounded sergeant keeps swimming until someone blows out his brains
After the fighting, only the warders, mates, and the doctor remain from the enemies
Eight of the group refuse to stand by while men are killed in cold blood
Prendergast orders a clean job and says he will not leave a tongue able to speak in a witness-box

communicates.speaker: prendergast
communicates.content: Our only chance of safety lay in making a clean job of it, said he, and he would not leave a tongue with power to wag in a witness-box.

events.label: Prendergast says the group may take a boat and go

communicates.speaker: prendergast
communicates.content: It nearly came to our sharing the fate of the prisoners, but at last he said that if we wished we might take a boat and go.

events.label: The group is given sailors' togs, a barrel of water, two casks, junk, biscuits, and a compass
Prendergast throws a chart to the group and tells them they are shipwrecked mariners whose ship foundered in lat. 15º N.

communicates.speaker: prendergast
communicates.content: Prendergast threw us over a chart, told us that we were shipwrecked mariners whose ship had foundered in lat. 15º N., and then cut the painter and let us go.

events.label: The barque draws slowly away from the boat after the seamen haul the foreyard aback and a light wind from the north and east persists
Evans and the narrator sit in the boat working out their position and planning what coast to make for
A dense black cloud of smoke shoots up from the barque and hangs in the sky line
A roar like thunder bursts and the Gloria Scott is no longer visible
The boat’s head is swept around and the group pulls hard toward the haze trailing over the water
A splintered boat and wreck fragments show where the vessel foundered, and a cry for help leads to a man on wreckage
The man Hudson is pulled aboard the boat
Prendergast and his gang proceed to put to death the five remaining prisoners
The two warders and the third mate are shot and thrown overboard
Prendergast cuts the throat of the surgeon in the 'tween-decks
The first mate kicks off loosened bonds and plunges into the after-hold
Convicts find the first mate with a match-box beside an open powder barrel and he threatens to blow all hands up

communicates.speaker: first_mate
communicates.content: swearing that he would blow all hands up if he were in any way molested.

events.label: An explosion occurs near the first mate by the powder barrel
Next day the brig Hotspur picks up the survivors
After landing at Sydney, Evans and the narrator change their names and go to the diggings
In the seaman who comes to them, the narrator recognises the man Hudson
Hudson tracks down the group and sets himself to live upon their fears
The narrator strives to keep peace with Hudson, noting Hudson has gone to another victim with threats
A shaky hand writes that Beddoes writes in cipher to say Hudson has told all, and asks for mercy on their souls
After the letter of warning is written, neither Beddoes nor Hudson is ever heard of again
No complaint is lodged with the police
Hudson is seen lurking about and police believe he has done away with Beddoes and fled
Beddoes revenges himself on Hudson and flees the country with money

clues.significance: Holmes inferred that Trevor had feared some personal danger within the last twelve months after observing and describing a stick he said had been bored and filled with melted lead so it could act as a formidable weapon.
Holmes inferred from visible tattoo initials J.A. on Victor Trevor's elbow and attempts to obliterate them that the initials had once been very familiar and Trevor had wished to forget them.
Watson remembered that Fordingbridge was in Hampshire and that Mr. Beddoes was also mentioned as living in Hampshire, linking the sender possibilities of the letter to Hudson and Beddoes.
The narrator presents the note as ciphered writing that says Hudson has told all.
